name: Klarna Group plc
sector: Finance / Digital bank & consumer credit (BNPL, Fair Financing, card)
moat_justification: Scale and distribution are real — 120M active consumers, 1.2M+ merchants, default-on distribution inside Stripe, Nexi, Worldpay and JPMorgan Payments, a Swedish banking licence with ~$13B of consumer deposits funding ~91% of the book — but there is no proven pricing power or through-cycle profitability behind it: operating income was negative in all three filed years (-$323M / -$121M / -$230M), ROE was -11.1% / +0.9% / -10.2%, the fundamentals.json roic_proxy is not meaningful for a deposit-funded lender (debt tags blank, deposits sit in liabilities), and the product is contestable by card networks, PayPal, Affirm, Afterpay and big-tech wallets with deeper capital. Narrow, contestable franchise: 4/10.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-26, EDGAR klar-20251231.htm): the registered security is the ordinary share itself; the company's IPO prospectus (Form F-1, declared effective 2025-09-09) and its IPO completion release state the offering was of ordinary shares at $40.00 per ordinary share and that the ordinary shares began trading on the New York Stock Exchange on September 10, 2025 under the symbol KLAR — there is no ADS programme and no depositary ratio) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
THIN_HISTORY: only 3 fiscal years of data

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share -3.29 vs 3-yr median 1.23 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier B (15.4%) vs bull-case tier A (23.4%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Contestable digital-bank franchise, moat 4/10 — the OCF numbers clear 15% (18.5% weighted, IV@15 $17.23 vs $13.08) but that base is a lender's balance-sheet artifact: payable earnings (profit attributable to ordinary equity holders: FY2024 $3M, FY2025 -$294M) run far below the $450M median OCF base, so the final tier is notched to C; on payable earnings it does not clear 15%.
tier_override_reason: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH softening (Andrew's standing rule, 2026-10-15): Klarna is a deposit-funded lender (SIC 6199, Swedish banking licence), so consolidated OCF capitalizes balance-sheet flows — deposit inflows and consumer-lending book movements — exactly as insurer OCF capitalizes float. The median OCF base is $450,000,000 total (FY2024 oe_conservative, financials_history.csv; $1.2349/share) against payable earnings — profit attributable to ordinary equity holders (statements.json net_income_to_common) — of $3,000,000 in that same FY2024 (consolidated net income $21,000,000 before non-controlling interests), a -$294,000,000 attributable loss in FY2025 (consolidated -$273,000,000) and adjusted operating profit of $65M in FY2025 (company release) — the median OCF base is ~150x FY2024's attributable profit, and no filed year shows attributable earnings within an order of magnitude of the base. Tier-by-numbers B (18.47% weighted IRR) therefore overstates distributable owner's earnings; sized down one notch to C, confidence low. The bear end of the band (15.4%) is the ceiling of what the numbers support, and on a payable-earnings base the name does not clear 15% at $13.08.
moat_for: Consumer scale: 120M active consumers and 1.2M+ merchants (Q2 2026 release), purchase-intent data from the shopping app
Distribution becoming default-on inside Stripe, Nexi, Worldpay and JPMorgan Payments, plus Walmart via OnePay and the Apple Upgrade programme
Swedish banking licence and ~$13B consumer deposits (~91% of funding) — cheaper, stickier funding than wholesale-funded BNPL rivals
AI-driven cost base: revenue per employee sharply up, headcount cut while GMV grew +22% in FY2025
moat_against: No demonstrated pricing power: merchant fees are contested by card schemes, PayPal, Affirm and Afterpay, and checkout placement must be re-won
Credit is the product: the fast-growing Fair Financing book (36-month loans) is unseasoned — provisions rose ~60% in FY2025 and flipped the P&L to a loss
No through-cycle returns: operating losses in all 3 filed years, ROE -11.1% / +0.9% / -10.2%; a moat that never shows up in earnings is unproven
Regulation cuts both ways (EU CCD, UK FCA, NY BNPL Act) and larger banks / big tech can replicate the offer with cheaper capital
